key_insight: TOCOMAS enforces topological coherence in multi-agent systems so task responsibilities, handoffs, and memory boundaries stay aligned with the underlying task graph.
engineering_relevance: This gives system builders a structured way to co-design agent roles, collaboration paths, and memory access policies for more reliable self-evolving multi-agent workflows.
method: Grounds the task graph in tool interfaces.
Groups compatible task nodes into reusable responsibility domains and derives dependency-driven collaboration.
Adds boundary-regulated memory visibility and only keeps self-evolution candidates that satisfy structural constraints and improve reward.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements over baselines on BBEH, WorkBench, SWE-Bench-Verified, and CoMemBench, including better verified progress, handoffs, and memory isolation on CoMemBench.
watch_item: The approach depends on correctly specifying structural constraints and task graphs, so performance may degrade if the graph or tool-interface mapping is inaccurate.
paper_title: Topological Coherence for Self-evolving Multi-agent Systems
